newsitem.title: USA: Clinton confidants knew of Hubbell's trouble - Times.
newsitem.headline: Clinton confidants knew of Hubbell's trouble - Times.

text.p: Two close confidants of President Clinton knew of the serious trouble Webster Hubbell faced even before he resigned as associate attorney general in 1994, the New York Times said Monday.
But the White House has said the Clintons did not know Hubbell faced possible criminal charges when their associates started organizing to help him, the newspaper said.

The Times, which cited documents and interviews, said Arkansas lawyer James Blair went to the Clintons to tell them Hubbell needed "to resign as quickly as possible," according to Blair's testimony before Senate Whitewater investigators.
The Clinton's personal lawyer David Kendall was also involved in the move to persuade Hubbell to resign, having similar information about Hubbell, the newspaper said.

Hubbell, once a close friend of Clinton's and a law partner of his wife Hillary Rodham Clinton, resigned amid controversy over his private law practice in early 1994. Later that year he pleaded guilty to fraudulent billing of clients at the Rose Law Firm in Little Rock, Arkansas, here he worked before joining the Clinton Administration.
